title: A Standing Forest: If the Past Had Been Different

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si hubiera* + participle with the simple conditional from B2 Unit 11 (the mixed conditional): *si hubiera* + participle for a past that did not happen, with the simple conditional for a result in the present (*Si hubiera estudiado, ahora sería médica*). It is the natural tool for "if we had ..., today there would be ...". Here it works on the Amazon and its standing-forest economy.

sections.title: A past cause, a present result
rows: Si no se hubieran talado tantos árboles en el siglo XX, hoy habría más bosque.
*si hubieran talado* ... *habría*: a different past, a different present
Si hubiera visitado Belém en octubre, ahora recordaría la procesión.
an imagined past visit, a present memory
Si hubiéramos protegido antes la selva, hoy tendríamos más árboles.
Si los exploradores no hubieran conocido la quina, hoy sabríamos menos sobre ese árbol.
a past event, a present result

items.spanish: Si el caucho no se hubiera producido en Asia, hoy Manaus quizá tendría otra economía.
items.english: If rubber had not been produced in Asia, Manaus might have a different economy today.

items.spanish: Si hubieras comprado castañas en Belém, ahora tendrías un buen recuerdo.
items.english: If you had bought nuts in Belém, you would have a good souvenir now.

items.spanish: Si no hubiera existido la minería, los ríos estarían hoy más limpios.
items.english: If mining had not existed, the rivers would be cleaner today.

sections.content: Look at the result: a word such as *hoy* or *ahora* means the simple conditional (*habría* + participle is for a past result). In the *si* clause *habría* never appears: *si hubiera estudiado*, not *si habría estudiado*. These are imagined situations, not facts.
